text_summary.body: Josiah commanded the people to keep the Passover as written in the book of the covenant; none like it had been kept since the days of the judges; it was kept in Jerusalem in Josiah's eighteenth year. Chronicles (35:1–19) adds the date, the fourteenth day of the first month, the return of the ark to the Temple, and the animals given: 30,000 lambs and kids and 3,000 bulls from the king, 2,600 and 300 from the priests' officials, 5,000 and 500 from the Levite chiefs.

setting.body: Lumby observes that Kings omits Hezekiah's passover (2 Chr 30) and reads the claim as about the complete form of the feast; Keil rejects squeezing the whole reform into the time before this Passover.

assumptions: The eighteenth regnal year begins 16–17 years after accession (non-accession count) or 17–18 years after (accession count) and lasts a year: offset 16–19 years from the start of the reign (operator margin).

competing_reconstructions.label: Passover in the same regnal year as the discovery
competing_reconstructions.summary: With a Nisan new year the discovery, covenant and purge would precede 14 Nisan of the same year; with a Tishri new year there could be up to six months. The text's calendar is not stated.

competing_reconstructions.label: LXX "in the eighth month" at 2 Kgs 22:3 as evidence for autumn regnal years
proponents: O. Thenius and E. Bertheau (as reported by Keil)
C. F. Keil (1872) rejects it as a "worthless gloss"
competing_reconstructions.summary: If the discovery fell in the eighth month of a Tishri-based year, there would be time before the Passover of the same regnal year; Keil argues the gloss proves nothing.

commentary.paraphrase: Guzik treats the Passover as a national observance restored after long neglect.

Guzik notes that Hezekiah's Passover had to be held in the second month, while Josiah's was on time; Selman counts more than double Hezekiah's offerings and notes that the Levites slaughtered the lambs.
